claim: Retrogradely labelled neurons from intermediate hippocampus were found in layer 3 of MEC.
source: As well as finding retrogradely labelled cell bodies in layer 3 of MEC, which contains neurons that are well established as a critical input to stratum lacunosum-moleculare of CA1 (Naber et al., 2001; Kitamura et al., 2014), we also found labelled cell bodies in L5a, which we identified by immunostaining against the ETS variant transcription factor-1 (Etv1) protein.
evidence: The manuscript describes retrograde labeling experiments showing labeled neurons in layer 3 of MEC, supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Layer 3 of MEC contains neurons that are a critical input to stratum lacunosum-moleculare of CA1.
source: As well as finding retrogradely labelled cell bodies in layer 3 of MEC, which contains neurons that are well established as a critical input to stratum lacunosum-moleculare of CA1 (Naber et al., 2001; Kitamura et al., 2014), we also found labelled cell bodies in L5a, which we identified by immunostaining against the ETS variant transcription factor-1 (Etv1) protein.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior published work (Naber et al., 2001; Kitamura et al., 2014).

evidence: The manuscript describes validation of the Rbp4-Cre line for targeting L5a, with citation to the source of the line.

claim: Axons from L5a neurons were primarily found in deep stratum pyramidale and stratum lacunosum of CA1.
source: In contrast to projections from superficial layers 2 and 3, which, respectively, target stratum lacunosum (SL) and stratum moleculare (SM) of CA1 (Kitamura et al., 2014), axons from L5a neurons were primarily found in deep stratum pyramidale (SP) and SL, but were sparse in SM (Figure 2A–D and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
